title: Grade 4 HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — Premium Revision Paper #14

pages.quiz:
HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #14
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which two elements are needed for a crop to grow well? (1 mark)
   A. Metal and stone
   B. Fire and metal
   C. Water and earth
   D. Space and salt

2. Which activity shows how to care for the environment? (1 mark)
   A. Cutting trees for fun
   B. Throwing rubbish out of a matatu
   C. Burning waste in the field
   D. Planting a tree in the school compound

3. The soil in a shamba belongs to which element? (1 mark)
   A. Agni
   B. Vayu
   C. Akash
   D. Prithvi

4. Tulsi leaves are offered to which gods? (1 mark)
   A. Lord Shiva only
   B. Guru Nanak
   C. Lord Vishnu and Lord Krishna
   D. Lord Mahavir

5. Which element is called Akash? (1 mark)
   A. Earth
   B. Space
   C. Water
   D. Fire

6. What lesson does the Narsimha story teach? (1 mark)
   A. Faith is useless
   B. Pride and cruelty do not last
   C. Kings never make mistakes
   D. Bullies always win

7. Which activity helps us remember the teachings of Enlightened Beings? (1 mark)
   A. Colouring the poster
   B. Acting a skit of a story
   C. Reading it silently
   D. Reading the story aloud twice

8. Match the being to the teaching. Which pair is correct? (1 mark)
   A. Guru Ram Das: Cruelty
   B. Parshvanath: Ahimsa
   C. Narsimha: Greed
   D. Buddha: Pride

9. In which city was Parshvanath born? (1 mark)
   A. Nairobi
   B. Varanasi
   C. Lumbini
   D. Lahore

10. At what time of day did Narsimha appear in the story? (1 mark)
   A. At noon
   B. At midnight
   C. At sunrise
   D. In the evening, between day and night

11. What was the name of Siddhartha's father? (1 mark)
   A. Guru Amar Das
   B. King Suddhodana
   C. King Dasharatha
   D. Hiranyakashipu

12. Which Tirthankar is the twenty-third of Jainism? (1 mark)
   A. Buddha
   B. Mahavir
   C. Parshvanath
   D. Guru Nanak

13. What was Guru Ram Das Ji's childhood name? (1 mark)
   A. Siddhartha
   B. Prahlad
   C. Ravi
   D. Jetha

14. Who took Ram and Lakshman to protect his forest prayers? (1 mark)
   A. Sage Vishwamitra
   B. King Shibi
   C. Guru Nanak
   D. Sage Valmiki

15. Whose hymns are also in Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji? (1 mark)
   A. Bhagat Kabir Ji and Bhagat Ravidas Ji
   B. Valmiki and Sigala
   C. Prahlad and Siddhartha
   D. Dasharatha and Ram

16. Which of the Sigalovada teachings shows how to treat the people who help us at home or work? (1 mark)
   A. Pay no attention
   B. Shout at them
   C. Ignore them
   D. Respect and care for workers and helpers

17. What does sakha mean in the prayer? (1 mark)
   A. Wealth
   B. Mother
   C. Friend
   D. God

18. From which Veda does the Gayatri Mantra come? (1 mark)
   A. Rig Veda
   B. Atharva Veda only
   C. Dhammapada
   D. Ramayan

19. Which prayer starts with the words Twameva mata cha pita twameva? (1 mark)
   A. Gayatri Mantra
   B. Saraswati Vandana
   C. Twameva Mata cha Pita Twameva
   D. Om Namah Shivaya

20. What is the purpose of a lost and found corner? (1 mark)
   A. To sell lost items
   B. To keep the items forever
   C. To keep found items until owners claim them
   D. To hide them

21. Why is integrity compared to a strong wall? (1 mark)
   A. Because it is tall
   B. One weak brick can make it fall
   C. Because walls are white
   D. Because it is heavy

22. Which is a sign of integrity? (1 mark)
   A. Keeping your promises
   B. Telling lies
   C. Taking a friend's pen
   D. Cheating in a test

23. What is a skit? (1 mark)
   A. A dance only
   B. A map
   C. A game with rules
   D. A short act showing a story

24. How should learners who return lost items be treated? (1 mark)
   A. They should be thanked
   B. They should be laughed at
   C. They should be punished
   D. They should be ignored

25. What does Kirat Karni mean? (1 mark)
   A. Fasting
   B. Travelling
   C. Earning by honest work
   D. Painting

26. What is the lesson of the Harishchandra story? (1 mark)
   A. Promises are not important
   B. Truth is worth more than wealth or comfort
   C. Lies are useful
   D. Wealth is everything

27. What does the word yoga mean? (1 mark)
   A. To sleep
   B. To join or unite
   C. To run
   D. To eat

28. Which is an activity for International Yoga Day? (1 mark)
   A. Playing loud music
   B. Skipping class
   C. Doing yoga together at school or a park
   D. Staying at home only

29. What should you practise yoga on? (1 mark)
   A. A tree
   B. A mat
   C. A wet floor
   D. A road

30. Which tradition teaches the five principles in this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. A trade union
   B. Only the Buddhist tradition
   C. Sanatan or Vedic
   D. A market

31. How does Namaste show the idea of Paramatma? (1 mark)
   A. It shows respect for the divine in everyone
   B. It is a food
   C. It means goodbye only
   D. It is a race

32. What does the Kiswahili word Madaraka mean? (1 mark)
   A. Peace
   B. Food
   C. Power or authority to govern
   D. Freedom of religion

33. Which Jain scripture is often read during Paryushan? (1 mark)
   A. Dhammapada
   B. Kalpasutra
   C. Ramayan
   D. Guru Granth Sahib

34. How can we help a friend who uses a wheelchair at a festival? (1 mark)
   A. Laugh
   B. Help them to move safely and include them
   C. Ignore them
   D. Leave them alone

35. In which year did Kenya gain internal self-government? (1 mark)
   A. 1980
   B. 2010
   C. 1950
   D. 1963

36. Which festival comes first in the year in the lesson's timeline? (1 mark)
   A. Maha Shivratri
   B. Jamhuri Day
   C. Paryushan
   D. Madaraka Day

37. What is the Indian name for Wednesday? (1 mark)
   A. Somvaar
   B. Budhvaar
   C. Guruvaar
   D. Shanivaar

38. What is a calendar? (1 mark)
   A. A festival
   B. A way of counting days, weeks and months
   C. A prayer
   D. A kind of map

39. Which two heavenly bodies besides the five planets are counted as grahas? (1 mark)
   A. The stars and clouds
   B. The Sun and Earth
   C. Earth and Pluto
   D. The Sun and the Moon

40. Which of these is a month of the Indian traditional calendar? (1 mark)
   A. January
   B. June
   C. Chaitra
   D. March

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Why should a passenger wait for the vehicle to stop before getting off? (2 marks)

42. Describe three rites and rituals in a Mandir. (3 marks)

43. What is a rite or ritual? Give one example. (2 marks)

44. Explain why a child should understand the meaning of a prayer. (4 marks)

45. Match each element to its Sanskrit name: earth, fire, air. (3 marks)

46. Describe how Paryushan Parva is celebrated. (3 marks)

47. Describe how Hindu families care for the Tulsi plant. (3 marks)

48. Explain why yoga should be practised with an expert. (4 marks)

49. Give two benefits of daily prayer. (2 marks)

50. List three things you should do before starting yoga. (3 marks)

51. Explain the Sikh idea of Kirat Karni. (2 marks)

52. List the five principles of Dharma studied in the lesson. (2 marks)

53. Why do the festival dates in this calendar change from year to year on our usual calendar? (2 marks)

54. Explain why respect for the holy books of other faiths is important in Kenya. (5 marks)

55. Explain how you can show integrity when using the internet. (3 marks)

56. Describe how to set up a lost and found corner in a classroom. (4 marks)

57. Explain the four Purusharthas with one example each for a child. (4 marks)

58. Write a weekly plan using English and Indian day names with one activity for each of three days. (5 marks)

59. Which day is Shanivaar and which planet is it linked with? (2 marks)

60. Why should children do Bhastrika and Kapaal Bhaati gently? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #14 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — Water and earth
   Soil and water help a crop to grow.

2. D — Planting a tree in the school compound
   Planting trees helps the environment.

3. D — Prithvi
   Soil is earth, or Prithvi.

4. C — Lord Vishnu and Lord Krishna
   Tulsi leaves are offered to Vishnu and Krishna.

5. B — Space
   Akash is the open sky or space that holds everything.

6. B — Pride and cruelty do not last
   Good defeats pride in the story.

7. B — Acting a skit of a story
   A skit helps us learn the lesson.

8. B — Parshvanath: Ahimsa
   Parshvanath is linked with non-violence.

9. B — Varanasi
   Parshvanath was born as a prince in Varanasi.

10. D — In the evening, between day and night
   It was neither day nor night but the time between.

11. B — King Suddhodana
   Siddhartha's father was King Suddhodana.

12. C — Parshvanath
   Parshvanath is the twenty-third Tirthankar.

13. D — Jetha
   His childhood name was Jetha.

14. A — Sage Vishwamitra
   Vishwamitra asked for their help.

15. A — Bhagat Kabir Ji and Bhagat Ravidas Ji
   It includes holy men of other traditions.

16. D — Respect and care for workers and helpers
   Workers are one of the six directions.

17. C — Friend
   Sakha means friend.

18. A — Rig Veda
   The Gayatri Mantra comes from the Rig Veda.

19. C — Twameva Mata cha Pita Twameva
   It begins with these words.

20. C — To keep found items until owners claim them
   Owners can claim their things.

21. B — One weak brick can make it fall
   Small lies can weaken trust.

22. A — Keeping your promises
   Keeping promises shows honesty.

23. D — A short act showing a story
   Skits help us learn lessons.

24. A — They should be thanked
   Thanking encourages honesty.

25. C — Earning by honest work
   Kirat Karni is honest labour.

26. B — Truth is worth more than wealth or comfort
   The king chose truth.

27. B — To join or unite
   Yoga joins body, breath and mind.

28. C — Doing yoga together at school or a park
   People do yoga together.

29. B — A mat
   A clean mat is best.

30. C — Sanatan or Vedic
   It is the ancient Hindu way.

31. A — It shows respect for the divine in everyone
   Namaste honours the divine in others.

32. C — Power or authority to govern
   It means authority to govern.

33. B — Kalpasutra
   Many Jains hear the Kalpasutra.

34. B — Help them to move safely and include them
   Inclusion is important.

35. D — 1963
   On 1 June 1963.

36. A — Maha Shivratri
   It is in February or March.

37. B — Budhvaar
   Budh is Mercury.

38. B — A way of counting days, weeks and months
   Calendars organise time.

39. D — The Sun and the Moon
   The seven days link to Sun, Moon and five planets.

40. C — Chaitra
   Chaitra is the first month.

SECTION B
----
41. (2 marks)
   Answer: Moving while the vehicle is moving can cause falls and accidents.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for danger, 1 mark for safety.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Darshan, aarti, prasad, bhajans, ringing the bell (any three, with a short description).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: A special action done in a set way at a festival, such as lighting a lamp or raising a flag.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meaning, 1 mark for example.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: Understanding makes the prayer come from the heart, helps us remember it, and helps us live by its message. Rushing without meaning makes it only a habit.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid point, up to 4.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Earth: Prithvi. Fire: Agni. Air: Vayu.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct pair.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: Jains fast, pray and meditate, listen to scriptures such as the Kalpasutra, practise Ahimsa, give to the needy and ask for forgiveness.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct practice, up to 3.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: They grow it in a pot or a stand in the courtyard, water it every morning, walk around it and pray. Its leaves are offered to Vishnu and Krishna and used in home medicine.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct point, up to 3.

48. (4 marks)
   Answer: An expert shows the correct posture, corrects mistakes, prevents strain of the back or knees, and knows when to stop.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for four points.

49. (2 marks)
   Answer: It helps us start the day calmly, teaches discipline, makes us thankful and gives peace of mind (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: Wear loose clothes, prepare a mat, have an empty stomach, find a quiet place, meet with a teacher (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

51. (2 marks)
   Answer: Earning a living by honest work.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for earning and 1 mark for honest work.

52. (2 marks)
   Answer: Paramatma, Purushartha, Prani Daya, Punarjanam, Prarthana (any correct set earns marks).
   Working / marking points: Half a mark for each, rounded up.

53. (2 marks)
   Answer: The months follow the Moon, so the dates move.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

54. (5 marks)
   Answer: Kenya has people of many faiths, and respect helps us live in peace and unity. Making fun of another's holy book hurts feelings and causes conflict. Listening and learning builds understanding.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for many faiths, 1 mark for peace and unity, 1 mark for hurt feelings, 1 mark for learning, 1 mark for a clear example.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: Ask permission before using a device, do not copy another's work, do not send unkind or untrue messages, and keep personal details private (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

56. (4 marks)
   Answer: Place a box or table in a safe place, write each item in a book with the date and finder's name, let owners claim their things, and thank those who return items.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for four points.

57. (4 marks)
   Answer: Dharma: doing homework and telling the truth. Artha: saving pocket money honestly. Kama: enjoying play and friendship. Moksha: praying and growing kind.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct pair.

58. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any correct plan, for example Somvaar: help at home; Guruvaar: thank a teacher; Shukravaar: share with a friend.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the format and 1 mark each for three correct day names with activities.

59. (2 marks)
   Answer: Saturday, linked with Saturn.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

60. (2 marks)
   Answer: They are active breathing exercises, so children need a teacher and must stop when tired.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.
